title: Three things to know about Sakamoto Days season two
excerpt:
Season two premieres on Netflix on January 18, 2027.
The trailer previews new action and a Creepy Nuts opening.
body_md:
Sakamoto Days is returning for a second season as part of the winter 2027 anime lineup. The adaptation of Yuto Suzuki's manga combines action and comedy with the story of a former assassin attempting to maintain a peaceful life. With the first season establishing its characters and central conflict, the upcoming episodes are expected to move into more consequential territory. Here are three important things to know before the premiere.

**1. Release date and episode format**

The second season is scheduled to premiere on Netflix on January 18, 2027. The platform remains the streaming home of the series, and viewers who have not finished the first season can catch up there before new episodes arrive.

The official episode count has not yet been announced. Season one was divided into two parts, but a comparable release structure has not been confirmed for the sequel. A single cour of approximately 12 or 13 episodes has been suggested as a possibility. That estimate remains speculation rather than an official production announcement, however, and the eventual format could differ.

**2. The next major chapter of the story**

Season two will continue the JCC Infiltration Arc, an important turning point in the original manga. Following the events of the first season, Taro Sakamoto and Shin seek additional information about Uzuki, whose activities threaten the peaceful existence that Sakamoto has attempted to build after leaving his former profession.

The upcoming season may also explore material from the arc focusing on Sakamoto's past. That section of the manga provides additional context for important characters and their relationships. Exactly how much of it will be adapted has not been established. Anime-only viewers can look forward to further development without needing to learn the details of those revelations in advance.

**3. A new opening theme and promising action footage**

The latest trailer confirms that the new opening theme, Papa wa Imada ni Juvenile, will be performed by Creepy Nuts. The group has become familiar to international anime audiences through music associated with popular productions including Dandadan and Mashle: Magic and Muscles.

The trailer has also generated discussion about the animation and fight choreography. Some manga readers criticized aspects of the first season's action sequences because of their expectations for Suzuki's source material. The new footage appears to emphasize dynamic movement and energetic combat, although a trailer cannot establish the quality of every finished episode.

With substantial story material still available to adapt, the second season represents an important opportunity to build on the first season's audience while addressing some of the concerns expressed by existing fans.
